rv.q: The play is so underwritten it is hard to distinguish between the fictional actor and the character she is playing.
She pours all of herself into Lily in one of those performances that seems so invested that you struggle to take your eyes off her.
An overstuffed, underpowered meta riff on La Voix Humaine
"I Can Die Too" is a fresh, captivating adaptation of the French early twentieth-century play "The Human Voice" whilst keeping its values at the core.
It may not flow seamlessly, nor fully mine the depth of the content it seeks to convey, but it is fun, impressively staged and energetically performed.
Ruffelle was a delight to watch on stage as Lily, bringing a wonderful comedic timing and also moments of softness; you couldn't get enough.
